Assignment 08 / Sculpting for Design

Moulding and Casting of Fruits and Vegetables

We explored how a fruit or vegetable could become a mould, then return as a cast in a different material.

Silicone moulds · Plaster · Clay · Resin

Group project with Astha Chand and Sudiksha Suresh

I worked with Astha Chand and Sudiksha Suresh to make moulds and casts in plaster, clay, and resin. We documented the process from building the mould to joining, repairing, and painting the finished pieces.

01

Making the mould

We began by building a mould around our fruit. Our photographs show the original orange, the silicone-lined mould, and the plaster support that held the parts together.

We had a scare when the silicone layers would not separate, but they had not finished setting. After two days, we were able to release the mould.

02

Learning where to stop the silicone

Our main mistake was spreading the silicone right to the edges. This could allow the layers to merge, making them difficult to separate. It also made it harder to mark where the mould halves should connect.

With the excess silicone, we also made a small experimental shape. It became a playful side study alongside the more structured casting process.

03

Casting in plaster

Small tears in the silicone caused minor deformations in our plaster cast. We also noticed a small gap when we joined the two halves.

After gluing the halves together, we used a very thin plaster paste to fill the gap and carefully removed the excess. The photographs show the mould halves, the unpainted form, and the finished orange.

04

Three attempts, then a clay cast

Clay was our hardest cast to make. We had three failed attempts before we finally got a result we could finish. Those attempts taught us to expect the unexpected when working with clay.

We kept photographs of the failed pieces as part of the process. The later images show the mould, the clay form, and the painted apple, keeping the unsuccessful attempts alongside the final result.

05

A cucumber in resin

Finally, we made a resin cast using a cucumber mould. We added appropriate markings so that the parts would join together correctly.

These images show the mould and the finished green cast. Marking the joining points addressed one of the difficulties we had encountered earlier when making the moulds.

06

The finished collection

Our painted orange, apple, and cucumber bring the three casting studies together. Each material introduced a different practical challenge, from repairing the plaster seam to learning through repeated attempts with clay.

We kept the process photographs with the finished pieces because the moulds, repairs, and failed attempts are part of what we learned.
